en/solve/solv-endless.title: A piece of the Internet on offline computers
en/solve/solv-endless.content:
If you’re reading this, it’s because, like me, you’re the type who can’t sit still and loves to “tinker” with computers to make them useful for more than just typing in Word.
I’ve spent many hours battling Dual Boot installations, partitions that get wiped, and USB drives that won’t boot. That’s why I want to lend you a hand so you can take “a piece of the internet” wherever it’s needed most, without failing in the attempt. Installing Endless OS is like stuffing a giant library into an old or new computer, and here I’ll explain how to do it like a pro tinkerer.
What is this solution for?
Endless OS isn’t just a program; it’s a complete Operating System → designed to work where the internet is a luxury. It comes with Wikipedia, cooking courses, health manuals, and educational games already downloaded. For a SOLE, it’s the perfect tool: it allows kids to look for answers to their Big Questions even if the router → is turned off.
What do you need for this mission?

A computer with Windows (which is where we’ll usually be “coexisting”).
Internet connection (only for the initial download).
A USB drive → of at least 32GB (if you’re going to use the memory stick method).
Disk space: At least 32GB free on the computer.
Plenty of patience and a desire to experiment.

How to do it?
1. The initial “Check-up”
Before downloading anything, check if the computer has space. In Windows, open the file explorer and make sure your “C: Drive” isn’t in the red. If you’re going to install the full version (the one with all the content), you need about 20GB to 32GB free.

Tinkerer’s tip: If the internet is really slow at the library, use a download manager like jdownloader. If the power or Wi-Fi cuts out, you won’t lose what you’ve already downloaded.

2. Download: Windows Installer or ISO Image?
If you go to the official Endless site, you’ll see two options:

Windows Installer: This is the easiest. It’s an .exe program that you install just like a game. It creates an automatic Dual Boot. When you turn on the PC, it will ask you: “Do you want to enter Windows or Endless?“.
ISO Image: This is for the more advanced folks. It allows you to create a USB that “formats” the PC or runs directly from the memory. You’ll need balenaEtcher to “burn” the ISO onto the USB. This option is good if the computer doesn’t have Windows or if you want to use Endless without touching the existing Windows installation.

3. The installation (The moment of truth)
If you use the Windows installer:

Double-click the file.
Select “Install alongside Windows”.
Choose the “Full” version. Don’t hesitate! The basic version is like a desert without internet; the Full version is the one that comes with Wikipedia and videos.
Let the PC do its thing. If it looks like it’s stuck at 99%, don’t turn it off. It’s moving heavy files.

4. The “Jump to BIOS” (If the USB doesn’t boot)
If you decided to use a USB and the computer ignores the memory and goes straight into Windows, you have to enter the BIOS/UEFI.

The trick: As soon as you turn on the PC, repeatedly press F2, F12, or Delete (it depends on the brand). Look for the “Boot” tab and put the USB first in the list.

Collective Glossary (To speak the same language)
As we agreed, we’ll build the meaning of these weird words we use here. If you find another one, write it down on the SOLE wall!

Operating System (OS): The main program that makes the computer work. Examples: Windows, Linux, Android, Endless OS.
Dual Boot: Having two operating systems on the same computer. When you turn it on, you choose which one to use. It’s like having a house with two doors.
ISO Image: A file that contains the entire operating system packaged up, ready to be “burned” onto a USB or DVD.
BIOS / UEFI: The most basic program on the computer that tells it what parts it has and which disk to boot from first.
Bootable USB: A USB drive prepared so the computer can boot (start) an operating system from it.
Partition: Dividing the hard drive into several “virtual” parts, as if you were putting up walls in a room so two people can live separately.

Final “Tinkerer” recommendations

Update before you leave: If you already have Endless installed and still have internet, open it and let it update. Once you’re out in the field (offline), you won’t be able to download new programs easily.
Test the search engine: Open the Endless search bar and type “Dinosaurs” or “Ozone layer.” If Wikipedia articles with photos pop up, you did it! You have a piece of the internet in your hands.
The forum is your friend: If something goes wrong, search Google for the error followed by the words “Endless OS forum.” There’s always someone who has already gone through that problem and left the solution behind.

How far can you go?
Having Endless is like having an offline library. It’s not the infinite internet of Google, but for looking up answers in a SOLE (How to do a SOLE? →), it’s a thousand times better than an empty computer.

en/solve/solv-express-invite.title: Learn how to design an express invitation without being an expert!
en/solve/solv-express-invite.summary: Invitations are key to gathering people.
en/solve/solv-express-invite.content:
Hi! I’m Manuela, and I’m not a professional designer, but that’s what cacharreo (tinkering) is all about: learning on your own and figuring things out by doing. I love designing, drawing, and creating. In fact, making collages is one of my favorite hobbies. Today, I’d like to share how to make an invitation based on my own experience.
Here, I’m going to talk mainly about the form, that is, how to make an invitation in general terms. You can also check out the solution How to write a good invitation? → if you are more interested in some recommendations regarding content.

What does it mean to design an invitation if you’re not an expert?
Have you ever felt like you don’t know how to make an invitation as pretty as the ones other people make?
Designing an invitation consists of choosing the graphic elements (like font color, accompanying images, etc.) through which you will make an invitation message eye-catching and attractive.
Invitations can be handmade or digital; choose whichever you prefer! In this solution, you will find tips for both. Shall we start?

💡 Remember that this solution is focused more on the form than the content. You don’t need to have design experience to start designing.


What is it for?
Very quickly: an invitation is used to summon people. When we organize activities or events that we want different people to attend, the invitation is the first contact we have with them and, therefore, the most important opportunity to grab their attention.
Whether by hand or using digital tools, you can create a powerful invitation. Keep reading and I’ll tell you how to make an excellent one.

What do you need?

If you are going to make your invitation digitally: a computer, tablet, or phone with Internet access.
If you are going to make it by hand: colored paper, colored pencils, markers, and felt-tip pens.
Creativity.
Freedom to express whatever you want.


How to do it?
Let’s start with analog → Your invitation by hand or with traditional techniques
To create your invitation by hand, keep this in mind:
Color: make it look pretty

Use colored paper or whatever you have on hand and start bringing your invitation to life using colored pencils, markers, or felt-tip pens.
Add creative details like decorative borders, simple illustrations, or symbols that represent the essence of your event. You can also think about using colored boxes to highlight information you think is valuable.
Play with different colors and shading techniques to make your design visually attractive and unique.

The text: say what’s necessary

Write the event details so they are easy to read. You can use your own handwriting or cut and paste printed letters from newspapers, magazines, posters… you can even make some with playdough or other materials you have on hand!
Use the resources from the previous section to highlight essential information.
Be creative with the text and make sure it’s clear for your guests. You can ask someone close to you for their opinion; several pairs of eyes always read better than just one.
Be careful not to overload it, otherwise, people might get lost in all that information… remember, ‘less is more’.

Review: a second look is always important

Review your design and add the finishing touches to perfect it; ask for opinions! I’m sure the input from people you trust will help.
Don’t forget to check the spelling of the words very carefully. A message that is well-written is understood well and leaves no room for confusion; remember that your goal is for people to understand everything clearly so they can attend what you are inviting them to.
If you want to get your invitation further, you can distribute it digitally: scan your creation or simply take a high-quality photo to distribute via messaging apps (email, WhatsApp, Telegram…) or social media.



Now, let’s go digital → Venture into trying the available technology
Log in to Canva
Canva is a design tool created so that anyone can use it. Open your browser and visit canva.com.
To start, you must have an account. If you don’t have one yet, you can create one for free. You just need an email address.

Select an invitation size
Once in Canva, choose the ideal size for your invitation. Canva offers many options to start with (for example, standard postcard size, social media post, etc.).
You can also customize the dimensions according to your needs using the “custom size” button.

Choose a template or start from scratch
A template is a pre-designed file, meaning someone else has already designed the content and you just need to edit it.
Do you prefer to start with a template or let your creativity fly from scratch? Use the search bar to explore the wide variety of options Canva offers and choose the style you like best:

Customize your design
Change the background and add elements like text, images, and decorations that represent the theme of your event. Experiment with different color combinations, fonts, and styles to make your invitation unique and exciting.
On the right side of the screen, you will find thousands of pre-designed graphic resources that you can choose and arrange as you please. In the “uploads” option, you can upload your own photos, videos (yours or from a link on the internet like YouTube), or audio.
Don’t be afraid to try new ideas and adjust the details until your design shines!
Look at how mine turned out:

Download your invitation
When you are happy with your design, click the “Share” button and select the “Download” option. Then, choose the format you want (usually JPG or PNG for images and PDF for longer files) and click the download button in the box that appears.

You can find your invitation in your computer’s “downloads” folder. If you can’t find it, use your computer’s file search tool to locate it.
Congratulations, your invitation is ready to print or share online! We hope this solution has been useful to you. If it was, share it with other people who you know could use it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

How to know if this solution works?
The easiest way to know is by asking for an outside opinion to make sure the invitation is clear and eye-catching. It is also useful to take a break or do another activity and then come back to review the invitation with “fresh eyes.” You can look at aspects such as:

Is the information clear enough (time, place…)? Is it easy to find and understand? Check the text, the font, and the layout of the text and image so it doesn’t look too cluttered.
Is it visually attractive, consistent with the event theme, does it grab attention, and generate interest?
Is the style aligned with the formality of the event and appropriate for the target audience?
Is it easy to share and view? Are the steps to follow or the “call to action” you are proposing clear?

After reviewing your invitation, it’s time for the “litmus test”: go ahead and share your invitation and see if people are interested in your activity or event.


⚠️⚠️ Remember: people not attending doesn’t always mean your invitation is the failure. Check if the time you scheduled it, the day of the week, the weather, or other external factors influenced the low attendance.


Other possible Internets
Summoning the people you’d like from a visual perspective. They say “you eat with your eyes first,” and in that, the form of an invitation is key.
The recommendations in this solution work for you, but you can also help others make theirs… or share the solution with those you think might need it.
Even if you aren’t an expert now, with practice, you surely will be! We hope it has been useful. Keep practicing; now you have more tools and inspiration to create increasingly memorable invitations!
See you soon! 👋🏽

en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.title: Does your community need financial support to connect to the Internet?
en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.summary: Some organizations offer low-cost Internet solutions.
en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. Although I didn’t write the original version of this solution, I’m reviewing it today so you can understand it better. Sometimes we feel like we’re all alone, swimming against the current. I want you to know that it doesn’t have to be that way, and that there are people and organizations out there who can help you. I hope this solution shows you some possible paths forward.
What is seeking financial support in your community to get connected to the Internet?
There are initiatives that aim to connect people who don’t have internet access, especially in rural, remote, and low-income areas.
They offer funding programs and resources for local communities and organizations that are working on building and expanding internet infrastructure, such as community networks and complementary access solutions.
Additionally, they provide information on how to get low-cost internet through government programs and non-profit organizations.

What is it for?
Reaching out to some of these groups could lead you to securing internet access for your community at affordable prices, with guarantees for maintenance, training, and sustainability that you might not even imagine right now… go for it!

What do you need?

A computer with a web browser and an internet connection.
A web translator like google translate, deepl, or an AI to help you translate (you can type “AI for text translation” into a search engine).
Patience and time to dedicate to the search; it’s better if you do it with others.
A dose of courage to send your request to one of these initiatives… we’re rooting for you! That’s how we did it.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Think of the best question you can ask the internet and dive in to find answers… you can do a SOLE!

In the case of Colombia, it could be something like “what initiatives connect rural, remote, and low-income communities to the internet in Colombia?”, or “how to get subsidized internet in Colombia?”, or “what organizations connect communities to low-cost internet in Colombia?” Be creative with your question to find a variety of answers!
You can also look at the search engine suggestions to dive deeper and find more related information.
Don’t be shy about contacting the companies and programs that the search engine suggests.


Step 2 → At SOLE Colombia, we know of some low-cost connectivity initiatives around the world. Take a look—we encourage you to get in touch with them!


Mintic - “Connecting the Unconnected” program by MINTIC and Colnodo

The “Connecting the Unconnected” program is an initiative by the Colombian Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) that seeks to bring the internet to rural areas and communities with little or no connectivity.
The Digital Centers are free Wi-Fi access points installed in strategic locations to facilitate internet access in these areas.
Steps to access, according to the program’s website:

Locate a Digital Center: Digital Centers are located in rural areas and communities with low connectivity. You can find information about their locations on the MinTIC website.
Turn on your device’s Wi-Fi: Turn on the Wi-Fi on your phone, tablet, or other device you want to connect.
Search for the “MinTIC Conecta” network: Your device will show available Wi-Fi networks. Select the network named “Mintic Conecta”.
Fill in the requested data: You will be asked to enter some information to register. Complete the required fields.
Accept the terms and conditions: Read the terms and conditions carefully and, if you agree, accept them to connect. You’re all set! Once you’ve completed the steps above, you’ll be able to use the internet connection.


Colnodo

In Colombia, access to the 900 MHz band for communities is being addressed through a public consultation led by the Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) and the National Spectrum Agency (ANE).
The goal is to make the use of this band more flexible for community networks, especially in rural areas with little or no commercial network coverage.
Process and Participation:

Public Consultation: A public consultation has been opened so that organized communities, community networks, and other interested parties can express their interest and provide comments on the proposal.
Participation Form: An online form is available for communities to describe their situation, interests, and suggestions regarding the use of the band.
Information and Documentation: The ANE has published documents and guidelines for the consultation, which can be viewed and downloaded.
Deadline: The public consultation is open until July 1, 2025.

Focus on Rural Areas:

The 900 MHz band, with its good coverage and penetration capacity, is considered ideal for supporting connectivity in rural and remote areas.
The aim is for community networks to be able to leverage this band to bring connectivity to places where there is no commercial coverage or where it is limited.

Potential Benefits:

Community Connectivity: Facilitating internet access for rural communities through community networks.
Economic and Social Development: Boosting access to services like telemedicine, virtual education, and other opportunities thanks to connectivity.
Community Empowerment: Community networks can build experience and autonomy in managing their own networks.
Future Readiness: Experience with this band can pave the way for adopting more advanced technologies and services in the future.

Active Participation:
It is crucial that interested communities actively participate in the public consultation, expressing their needs, expectations, and proposals for the use of the 900 MHz band. Participation from all interested sectors is fundamental to building a strategy that guarantees fair and sustainable connectivity for everyone.
In short, the 900 MHz band represents an opportunity for Colombian communities to access the internet and improve their connectivity, especially in rural areas, through community networks.
The public consultation is the space for communities to express their needs and contribute to building a public policy that recognizes the importance of the spectrum for social and economic development.

Internet Society

Offers funding to organizations that build and expand internet networks in underserved areas, which can result in more affordable options for residents.
Supports the creation of community networks, which are often a more economical alternative to commercial options.

NUPEF

NUPEF.org, through its focus on community networks and affordable internet access, can facilitate access to funding and resources to build or strengthen community internet networks, in addition to offering training to manage and maintain these networks.
It also promotes the creation of safe and inclusive virtual communities, empowering marginalized groups to use technology and advocate for their digital rights:


It can help you apply for grants and funding for community network projects, including building new access solutions or expanding existing ones, especially for marginalized and underserved populations.


Offers training and resources so community members can develop skills in building, managing, and maintaining community networks.


If you already have a network, NUPEF can help strengthen it by improving infrastructure, updating technology, and providing technical support to ensure its continuous operation.


Promotes the creation of safe and welcoming online communities where diversity is valued and users are protected from violence and abuse.


Works so that excluded people can use and adapt the internet and digital technology for their needs, including developing fair and equitable solutions for universal access.


Seeks economic models that allow for affordable and sustainable internet access, generating value in the community and promoting self-sufficiency.


Facilitates the exchange of knowledge and experiences between different communities and movements, promoting collective action for digital inclusion.


APC


It is a network of civil society organizations that helps people access the internet where there is no connectivity or it is not affordable.
It also supports local and grassroots groups so they can use technology to develop their communities and advance the defense and exercise of their rights.
Promotes government ICT policies that serve the interests of the population, especially in the context of the Global South.

Unconnected

It is an initiative that seeks to connect people who do not have internet access, especially in rural, remote, and low-income areas.
They offer funding programs and resources for local communities and organizations that are working on building and expanding internet infrastructure, such as community networks and complementary access solutions.
Additionally, they provide information on how to get low-cost internet through government programs and non-profit organizations.

High Speed Internet

If you know of any other way to get support to connect your community to low-cost internet, don’t forget to comment on this Solution so we can add it. We also ask that if you see this solution is outdated or contains incorrect information, let us know so we can keep researching and bringing this information to the ends of the earth.

How to know if this solution works?
How having low-cost internet can help:

Funding for infrastructure: there are organizations that offer funding to organizations that build and expand internet networks in underserved areas, which can result in more affordable options for residents.
Information on subsidy programs: other organizations provide information on government and non-government programs that offer subsidies or reduced rates for internet access for low-income individuals.
Community networks: others support the creation of community networks, which are often a more economical alternative to commercial options.
Resources to build networks: some others offer a toolkit for building and maintaining community networks, which can help reduce infrastructure costs.
Training for the installation and maintenance of equipment and networks.
Strengthening the social fabric and bonds between the community and the community of practice: initiatives usually include content and practice in digital rights, equity, community ties, and human connection, which make the internet an excuse to have more conscious and connected communities.


Other possible Internets
The continuous search for Internet Solutions has led us at SOLE Colombia to investigate and be curious about finding the “parceros” (partners/friends) who have helped us bring the internet to very remote places.
In that same way, you—yes, you—having access to this information, can feel encouraged to explore relationships with people and organizations that can guarantee the right that you and your community have to access the internet wherever you are.
When people come together to achieve things, the sky is the limit.

en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.title: How to obtain spaces with the help of allies?
en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.summary: Connect with institutions, NGOs, or others that have the capacity to manage spaces
en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.content:
Hi! I’m Catalina, welcome 👋🏽
This solution was written by Nicolás and Belén. Later, an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant helped me organize it according to the sections we always use as a guide, and finally, here I am, adding the experience and warmth that characterizes Voltaje ⚡⚡ solutions.
Sometimes it’s relatively easy to find meeting spaces in our community. Other times it’s not, either because they don’t know us or because it’s simply not easy to reach the people who manage them. In this solution, we’ve gathered some recommendations for managing spaces through allies—that is, other organizations or people who have closer access to the space you need.

Remember that you don’t always have to solve things on your own. At the end of the day, managing these spaces, like many other things, is really about weaving trust; about creating bonds. So, let’s get started!

What is getting spaces with the help of allies?
It’s the process of identifying, talking to, and reaching agreements with organizations that “guard” places (NGOs, foundations, libraries) so they can lend them to you, transforming them into environments where the community can meet and learn using the Internet as a group.
Getting spaces through allies isn’t just about paperwork (though it usually involves some of that) or the place itself. It’s more about the way you get someone excited about what you do, how you make them feel that it’s worth lending you their space or helping you manage one because they believe in your mission.
Here, I’ll talk mainly about physical space, but you can also check out another solution where we tell you how to mobilize others with your cause.

What is it for?
A space to connect to the Internet is an opportunity to turn it into a place for exchange with the community; a place to support one another and open doors to the world. Since it’s not always easy to find one on your own, the recommendations you find here can be helpful so you don’t have to walk this path alone.
But beyond just getting a space, weaving bonds with others is something that will allow you to collaborate in different ways in the future—not just to manage spaces or anything else, but to keep building a more equitable and beautiful world, one Big Question at a time.
Imagine your ally getting excited to create their own learning sessions using the Internet in a group after seeing you and your community in action!

What do you need?

A good purpose that explains why you want the space.
Patience, because bonds of trust are slow-cooked.
Courage to put yourself out there and talk to people who aren’t expecting you.


How to do it?

Recommendation #1 → Recognize the local stakeholders

There are many public and private institutions working in the territories where we live: governments, NGOs, cooperatives, foundations, among others.
Before knocking on a door, observe who is already there. Talk to your neighbors about past social projects. Ask at the school or the mayor’s office which organizations have a presence in the area.
Write it all down. It could be in a notebook or on a bulletin board with colorful sticky notes to distinguish one actor from another. The key is to make your directory as rich as possible.

⚠️💬 Keep in mind that in your search, it’s also important to know what stories have already been told or what other organizations or collectives have already participated in the spaces you identify. It’s always compelling to mention how your proposal can add to what others are already building.



Recommendation #2 → Reach out with purpose

Once you recognize who you’d like to approach, it’s time to do it!
As much as possible, always try to make contact in person. In-person meetings tend to be more effective than emails or letters. Once you manage to contact the person from this institution or organization, tell them about your projects and the difficulties you face in finding suitable spaces to gather your community.
When your search has a brave and powerful purpose, it’s easier to get what you need. If your intention is to host a SOLE, then you can share how any place can become a Self-Organized Learning Environment and how this allows people to discover ways to learn when there are no teachers around.

Remember that when your search is born from a genuine need of the community, doors tend to open more easily.



Recommendation #3 → Cultivate autonomy and trust

Once you’ve spoken with several stakeholders and identified which one you have the most affinity with and want to work with, see if you can speak on behalf of their institution or organization to manage the spaces that work for you, since the person won’t be able to accompany you every time you need to borrow it. Of course, give this time; first, allow a bond of trust to be generated with that person by showing them how your collective, organization, or community is autonomous and responsible.
Once you have their support and/or authorization, start the formal request for the spaces you’ve identified as most convenient for your community’s activities.
If you have to write a letter to request the space and don’t know how, go to the solution How to get a community hall or any community space to use the internet in a group? or How to write an invitation that brings people together?, you’ll surely find some help 💪🏽

How do you know if this solution is working?
The moment you manage to secure a space thanks to the company or support of another person, you will have achieved part of the initial goal!
Then comes the second part: when the space(s) stop feeling like “someone else’s” and start being recognized by the community as places for meeting and learning, you will have reached the maximum potential of this solution!

Other possible Internets
Managing spaces through others doesn’t just promote the creation of networks and collaborative work.
It also allows for building bridges between institutions and communities, making resources that were previously closed to the public become common goods for everyone’s learning.
The moment we transcend individuality and, for example, gather to learn together using the Internet as a group, we continue to create other possible Internets.

en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.title: Which free networks are available to connect to the internet?
en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.summary: Search for WiFi signals around you with a mobile application
en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.content:
Hi! I’m Belén, and I’d like to welcome you. I didn’t write this solution myself, but I’m going to walk you through it, and I’d love it if, by the end, you could tell me if you liked it, if it helped you, and if you were able to put it to use in your own neck of the woods.
What is scanning for nearby WiFi signals with a mobile app?
Scanning for WiFi signals → with a mobile app means using software on your smartphone to scan, analyze, and find wireless networks available right where you are. Often, you might think you don’t have Internet → or that your mobile signal is weak (which depends on the service your provider offers in your area), but if you look closely, there might be a WiFi network with a better connection or even a free one nearby.

What is it for?
Sometimes, the place where we are might not have access to Internet, but if we move around and head to a nearby spot, we might just find some WiFi networks. Even if we find them, we sometimes can’t access them because we don’t have the passwords.
The WiFi Map app shows us a map with WiFi networks within a 2-kilometer radius, based on your device’s location, and shares the access passwords with us. The networks saved in this app can be public or private.
If you want to make the most of a nearby connection, you can connect to those networks to use them as a group using SOLE. You only need a few devices, four or five people eager to learn per device, and Big Questions to solve. Want to know more about how to do a SOLE? Check out how to do it here: How to do a SOLE? - Tutorial

What do you need?

A Smartphone →
Available storage space on your phone
A mobile data connection
A bit of generosity


How do you do it?

Step 1 → Install the app


Before starting the installation process, you need to have a stable Internet connection.
Once you’ve got that, open the “Google Play” store for Android or the Apple Store for iOS and search for the WiFi Map app.
Another option is to click on one of these links using a web browser: Google Play and Apple Store




Step 2 → Set up the app

Once the app is installed, open it and accept the terms of use. It is very important that you grant it access to your location while the app is in use.

Open the app and swipe down from the top of your phone to access the control panel. Turn on your location if the app hasn’t already done so.


Step 3 → Use the app

When it shows you a map of the world, tap the “arrowhead” icon, and the map will center on your current region.
At the bottom of the screen, the closest WiFi networks for which we have the access password will appear.





Step 4 → Select a network


When you can see the list of WiFi networks nearby, you can select one to see its access details.
Sometimes the app will ask you to watch a video before letting you see the network passwords. This is how the app uses ads to fund itself in its free version.
Sometimes the app will ask you to watch a video before letting you see the network passwords. This is how the app uses ads to fund itself in its free version.





How do you know if this solution works?
With this recipe, you can access multiple WiFi networks, both public and private. In cities or urban centers, you’ll have many more chances to find networks with available access data compared to smaller, more remote towns.
Now, with a WiFi network, you’ll have more stability and speed to connect to the Internet—and why not use it to find answers to your Big Questions, learn something new, take courses, or share the resource with others?
Are you ready to get started?

Other possible Internets
This solution will allow you to have temporary Internet access, mainly in towns where users like you have shared access data for public or private Internet networks.
To access these passwords, you must have an internet connection, as only the paid version of the app allows you to download the map with the access information.

en/solve/solv-fish-game.title: How to use games to learn how to take care of equipment as a community?
en/solve/solv-fish-game.summary: A governance solution for managing common resources.
en/solve/solv-fish-game.content:
A governance solution for common resources
Solution video
You can watch this video while you work through this solution.

Hi, my name is Mateo and I’ll be your guide for this solution. If you’re here, it’s because you’re interested in knowing how to take care of and use the tech equipment that belongs to your community or work team. In this case, when we talk about tech equipment, we mean computers, antennas, tablets, data plans, etc.—any material asset that doesn’t belong to one person in particular, but to a community or group of people.

💡 Inspiration! At SOLE Colombia, we want more people to use the internet and tech equipment as a group, because it brings many benefits:

Using it together is more fun and invites us to share ideas.
It’s more economical and encourages teamwork.
When there’s someone else by your side, you’re less likely to fall for malicious websites or cyber scams.


What does it mean to use games to learn how to care for equipment as a community?
We develop teamwork skills, learn to value collective responsibility, and understand the importance of cooperating for the common good in a supportive environment. An excellent strategy for doing this is through games and participatory activities.
What is this solution for?
To start, you might be surprised if I tell you we don’t want to give you magic formulas on how to care for and use tech equipment as a community, because we don’t know the ins and outs of where you live and we understand that every context is different. However, we do have a fun and deep game that will allow you to reach agreements with your community or work team, called the Fish Game. With this game, we hope your community reflects on the care, distribution, and management of common resources on planet Earth, while discussing how to reach agreements for the shared use of the equipment you have at your disposal.
What do you need?

You need a bag with at least 80 candies, beans, or tokens of the same size to represent the fish in the game.
A table.
Chairs surrounding the table.
Large poster board (pliego).
Markers.

How to do it?


Moment 1: first game


💡 For the first game, place 50 of the 80 fish in the center of a table and tell the participants: “There are 50 fish in a lake and you are the fishers. To fish, you must follow these instructions:
a. Each person can catch between 0 and 5 fish per round.
b. You cannot speak; you can only use body language.
c. The fish reproduce: 1 new fish is born for every 10 fish remaining on the table after the round ends. Example: if 30 fish remain on the table, you must add three new fish.
d. You decide when the game ends.”
After giving the instructions, leave the bag with the 30 extra fish on the table and verify that each person has their moment to decide how many fish they are going to take.
At the end of the round, ask the players to return the fish and ask the group:

How did you feel about the distribution of the fish? Does it seem fair to you?






Moment 2: second game


💡 For the second game, the conditions change, so explain the following instructions out loud: “Now there are 50 fish in a lake and you are still the fishers, the difference is that you are in a drought, so fishing is much harder. There is a lot of scarcity and you must ensure food to feed your families in the coming weeks.”
The rules of the game are the same. Remind the participants of the rules if necessary.
At the end of the round, ask them:


What changed now? How do you feel about the distribution?


Do you think there could be similar difficulties when sharing your community’s tech equipment?


Moment 3: third game


💡 For the third game, the situation is the same as the second game, but the instructions change: “There are 50 fish in a lake and you are still the fishers, the difference is that you are in a drought, so fishing is much harder. There is a lot of scarcity and you must ensure food to feed your families in the coming weeks. There isn’t much time, so you must make quick decisions.”
a. Each person can catch between 0 and 5 fish per round.
b. You can talk for 2 minutes before fishing to decide the best way to do it.
c. The fish reproduce: 1 new fish is born for every 10 fish remaining on the table after the round ends. Example: if 30 fish remain on the table, you must add three new fish.
d. You decide when the game ends.”
At the end of the round, ask the participants:


Did the agreement you reached at the beginning of the game change anything?


Which of the games do you think had a fairer distribution? What are the differences between the three games?


How could the agreement you made be applied to the use and care of the tech equipment you have at your disposal?


Moment 4: the secret to reaching agreements


💡 Tell people the secrets of the game for reaching agreements:

The fishers represent each person in your community.
The fish represent the finite resources or tech equipment available to the community, for example, computers, internet antennas, data plans, etc. These fish also serve as an analogy for managing finite resources like land, water, food, or the air we breathe.

The key to this game is that the more fish we take for ourselves, the fewer fish will reproduce; so we all lose.
Likewise, the fewer fish we take, the more fish will reproduce on the table and the community will have more resources.



Moment 5: let’s reach an agreement

Give the participants the poster board and markers. Invite them to write down agreements on how to manage the resources or tech equipment they have at their disposal. We recommend downloading the following template to guide your conversation.
Rules for shared use and care of tech equipment.pptx
These questions are just a guide, so you can add or remove questions as you see fit. Ask the participants to put the agreements they reached in writing and invite them to share them with the rest of the community. This is fundamental because, in moments of conflict or difficulty in solving a problem, you can return to what was written to reach solutions or to rethink new agreements.
How does the game work?
First game: in the first game, people tend to consume fish based on their own interests and the behavior of others. If one person consumes many fish (5), the others tend to feel driven to consume the same amount; the same applies in reverse: if one person consumes few fish, the others (with some exceptions) tend to be motivated to consume less. Now, there are no magic formulas, and the future isn’t written regarding what might happen; the key is to observe people’s behaviors, as this will allow you to have powerful reflections on the responsible and communal management of finite resources.
Second game: due to the conditioning of the drought and the urgency of feeding the family, in the second game, people tend to consume more than in the first and third, which causes the distribution of fish to be more inequitable and run out faster. In other words, more tension is generated between personal benefit and common benefit. In behavioral psychology, this situation is called present bias: human beings, upon feeling that a resource is about to run out, activate a sense of loss that drives us to consume irrationally even when we don’t need to.
Third game: by this point, participants usually reach agreements to consume fewer fish so that more reproduce, preventing situations of scarcity and finding community alternatives for the equitable and fair management of resources; however, it is possible that this won’t happen. The important thing is that you tell them about the value of reaching agreements in the management of finite resources or tech equipment. When we reach agreements, we can all benefit; conversely, when we all seek our own personal benefits, the resources we could benefit from tend to be destroyed, as does our opportunity to continue benefiting from them.
How much is enough? The tragedy of the commons
The tragedy of the commons is a problem regarding social relationships and human behavior described by Garrett Hardin in 1968 for the journal Science, in which he proposes a thought experiment imagining a farmer who decides, on land shared with other farmers, to start adding more cows, since it generates more profit and personal benefits. The other farmers decide to do the same, so the field becomes full of cows, the land is overexploited, and it deteriorates rapidly. Likewise, the farmers are left with many cows but no land to produce on. This dilemma shows how we can destroy shared finite resources if each of us seeks only personal benefit, and it invites us to think about the importance of reaching agreements regarding shared resources.
Reaching agreements really works!
We want to share the story of Alexander, a community leader from the vereda in Agrado, located in the Department of Cauca. Alexander, together with his community, managed to reach an agreement on how to use the internet through a deal they made with the shop located next to the community hall. Let’s listen to his story:

en/solve/solv-full-server.title: "How to create your own Pocket Server (Full Server)?"
en/solve/solv-full-server.summary: "Extend the capabilities of your local network with a file manager and support for PHP applications."
en/solve/solv-full-server.content:
Hi there! I’m David. This solution is the natural evolution of the Pocket Internet → or giving a second life to an old computer →. Here, we’re going to turn that rig into a robust server capable of managing files and more complex applications.

What’s it for?
By setting up a “Full” server →, you’re giving your community a digital meeting point where they can easily upload and download files—like a local cloud, but without needing the internet. It’s a toolkit that can be passed from hand to hand via a USB connection →.

An analogy to help you get it (Possibility)
If it helps to visualize it, think of this server as a Community Kitchen:

The RAM memory → is the prep counter where you get the information ready.
The Storage → is the pantry where you keep the ingredients (files) for the long haul.
This server is the space where everyone can come to look for “recipes” (information) or drop off their own ingredients.


What do you need?

A computer with Linux → or a Raspberry Pi →.
Internet connection (only for the initial setup).
A USB flash drive →.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Connect via Terminal

Access your machine through a Terminal → using SSH →.


Step 2 → Create the public directory

We’re going to define the folder where all the shared information will live:
mkdir www
chmod 777 www


Step 3 → Install application support (PHP)

We’ll install the necessary packages so the server can run dynamic web applications:
sudo apt install php-fpm php-mbstring php-mysql php-curl php-gd php-zip php-xml -y


Step 4 → Configure the web server

You need to tweak the Nginx → configuration so it recognizes the new folder and the PHP language. This is done in the /etc/nginx/sites-available/default file.


Step 5 → Install the File Manager (Tiny File Manager)

So that anyone can upload files from their browser without needing to touch code, we’ll install this tool:
cd www
wget raw.githubusercontent.com/prasathmani/tinyfilemanager.php


Future possibilities (Under construction)
This solution opens doors to bigger projects we’re currently documenting:

Hand-to-Hand Replication: How to copy this entire system onto a USB drive so another community can use it just as easily.
Local AI and Agents: The possibility of having a smart assistant that summarizes texts or helps with tasks, running directly from your server’s RAM memory → without the internet.
AI-driven processes: Optimizing how information is organized using small, local artificial brains.


How to know if it works?
Visit solevoltaje.local/tinyfilemanager.php. If you can see the file manager, your server is ready for action!

en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.title: How to collect financial resources as a community?
en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.summary: Organize a collection to pay for community internet.
en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay, and one of my big ventures is putting the resources we have available to community use. I like to tinker—cacharrear, as we say—but I’m also interested in the ways we humans coordinate ourselves to live better together.
What is a fundraiser for community internet?
This solution gathers ideas on how to collect money to pay for a community connection—that is, getting a community to agree to financially sustain a resource that will be used and enjoyed by everyone.

What is it for?
Finding ways to organize ourselves to acquire things that improve our living conditions is sometimes a complex task.
If you’re clear that you need the internet, but you don’t know how to get your community on board, how to get them to back you on the maintenance and sustainability of the contract, or you don’t know the steps to take to make it happen together, you can find useful guidance in this solution.

What do you need?

A very clear idea of why you want to collect the money.
Charisma, a silver tongue, and people skills to convince others to participate in the fundraiser.
Orderliness to keep the books, manage the money, and keep those who contribute informed about the progress of the collection and the status of the accounts.
Communication skills to keep contributors informed about the service status, maintenance needs, or any issues. Also, to receive suggestions or handle the paperwork required to formalize or maintain the service.


How to do it?
These recommendations are relevant when running fundraisers for community purposes. They don’t necessarily have to be followed in order, nor are they the only ones, but we believe they can help you.

Step 1 → Moment 1: Let’s build a team; it’s easier with others

Find partners to start this campaign.
When we undertake projects for the common good, it’s easy to find allies to share responsibilities with. When you do these kinds of initiatives alone, you can quickly get tired and give up, but with others, this project will be much more manageable.
Define who will be in charge of what; that will make the work more organized and allow you to follow up more easily.


Step 2 → Give the fundraiser a purpose—one that is clear and gets us excited

It’s important to take the time to reflect and project what we want to do. What is it that we want to achieve? Remember, money is just a means to reach something bigger and more important… that’s called a purpose.
In this case, what is it that unites us in this fundraiser, that inspires us to move to raise the funds? When you are establishing the purpose of any project, it’s time to tirelessly ask ourselves why, until we are convinced.
Doing a SOLE is a great way to find a purpose for the fundraiser. Besides paying for it together, you can learn, dialogue, and create flourishing communities by using the internet as a group. Paying for the internet together allows you to use it for SOLE, or for anything else you can think of!
For example:

Why do we want internet in a public access space? So that people in my community can learn new things they need or want to learn, converse and dialogue with other people and communities in a Great Conversation, and take action in a self-organized way to live better together.
Why do we want people in our community to be able to learn together? So that it’s not necessary to depend exclusively on learning spaces and people related to the educational system, to realize that anyone can learn anything using the internet. Why as a group? Because going anywhere alone is a difficult path; on the other hand, when we do it together, it’s better.
Why do we want them to be able to converse via the internet? Interacting with other people with the goal of learning or letting others be part of our lives always makes us feel better. Learning together when there are other people participating in our discoveries and with whom we can walk the path together makes us feel that what we learn transcends and is bigger than us. If we connect with each other through the internet, it’s because we are mutually interested and can accompany each other; we aren’t alone on the path… Do you want to connect with people around the world in your SOLE sessions? Take a look at The SOLE Granny Cloud! They are volunteers from all over the world who connect to SOLE sessions to accompany, offer warm encouragement, share, learn, and have fun together.
Why do we want to help our community flourish? So that we can all have a happier, more complete, and sabrosa (delightful) life!

Does it make sense to have public access internet in our community? Absolutely!


Step 3 → Identify potential participants

Which of our neighbors would be interested in having community internet? What interest might they have in contributing money to this project? This way, we can translate our project into their potential interests.
Here are some examples of SOLEros who have self-organized to learn together using the internet:

Elainer, when she used SOLE so that the young people in her community could learn to make video games.
Robinson, who used SOLE so his community could find sustainable alternatives to their traditional crops.
María, when, through SOLE, she got her students to take responsibility for their own educational process and changed the way they research and learn at their school.




Step 4 → A story, the best way to communicate an idea

Now that we know who we are targeting with our campaign, let’s create a story. We recommend answering five fundamental questions: who, what, when, where, and why.
Here is ours:
In the community of La Piche, delicious honey is harvested. Everyone in the community works in trades related to the production of this delicious honey: some have hives, others collect the honey, others market it, some manufacture related products…
We are a group of young people interested in creating natural cosmetic products based on honey and beeswax, but we don’t know how to start manufacturing those products, what tools we need, what permits we require, or how we could market them, etc. We want to start with: how can we make a honey and beeswax lipstick?
Using the internet, we could find answers to these and other Great Questions!
The cheapest internet plan is $120,000 COP; no one in the village could pay for it alone. But we have thought that by collecting money among 12 people or families, we could pay a monthly fee of $10,000 COP and put the fiber-optic broadband internet in a place that is easily accessible to everyone, such as the nursing home, the community hall, or Doña Adela’s shop, which is the business that is open most of the time and where we could all connect. We could all use the connection, even the children in the village, to do their homework.
So, if you are interested and can be part of this fundraiser, add yourself to this list! Soon we will be able to have internet for ourselves!
I will send all expenses and bill payments on the first of every month to a WhatsApp → group, and through there, we can stay up to date on any news.
Are you joining the cause?


Step 5 → Purchase, communicate, and organize expenses

With the money collected, you just have to make the purchase.
Remember that none of these contracts have mandatory long-term clauses, so if you aren’t satisfied with the service, you can cancel it and switch to another provider.
It is important to be organized with the accounts and communicate payments and any news or issues immediately to everyone involved.
This way, everyone can take co-responsibility for any decision regarding this fundraiser and share the responsibilities or consequences.
Make sure to create a communication flow with your collaborators so you can communicate in both directions and quickly solve any problems that may arise.

How to know if this solution works?
With this solution, you manage to organize neighbors toward a common good, embodied in the payment of a service, to take advantage of it collectively and get the most out of it.
You also manage to improve the connectivity conditions of the place where we live, making it a place where life is better.

Other possible Internets
Organizing ourselves to get things done will take us as far as we want to go.
In this case, it allows us to have a shared internet point with public access. It is important to measure the bandwidth → offered by the service to be contracted very well. This way, we can contract a service that is fast and powerful enough in relation to the number of people we want to link to that connection.
The next step would be how to improve the conditions of this connectivity without a significant increase in costs.

en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.title: How to improve my mobile signal with a can?
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.summary: Make a small antenna for your cell phone.
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.content:
Hi! It’s a pleasure to meet you. My name is Mateo, and I’ll be walking you through this solution. If you’re reading, listening to, or watching this, it’s because you’re interested or curious about how to boost your cell phone signal in a very simple way. If that’s the case, you’re in the right place.

What is this solution for?
This solution helps improve your cell phone signal temporarily. In other words, it helps boost it, but keep in mind that signal quality also depends on external factors like the weather, the conditions of the place where you are, your carrier, and the number of towers emitting radio waves around you to allow for calls or internet browsing.
The solution I’m sharing with you is a simple, quick, and very interesting option. You’ll see that the results of this test are exciting and eye-opening.

What do you need?


One person is enough to work on this solution. Although everything is easier with company. Go for it!
A clean metal can, like one from a drink.
Scissors.
Utility knife (optional).
A ruler, preferably metal.
A fine-tip marker.
Thick transparent tape.
Safety gloves.


Before you start, some safety tips
Even though this solution has a basic difficulty level, it’s important to keep some recommendations in mind for your safety:

Work on a flat, rigid surface, preferably a table where you can cut.
Find a clean can that isn’t rusty.
We recommend being in a quiet place, free of distractions, and having as much time and patience as possible.
Keep your hands at a safe distance from the cuts you’ll be making with the scissors or utility knife.
Preferably, wear safety gloves.
We recommend sitting in a comfortable place to work.


How to do it?
This solution has 3 steps that I will guide you through. Keep in mind that some of them might be frustrating and others very exciting, and both are okay; they’re part of the “tinkering” process. The important thing is to keep trying. Let’s get started!

Step 1 → Draw the base metal sheet

To start, prepare all the materials mentioned.
Next, cut the base and the top of the can with the scissors or utility knife so that you have an open sheet; imagine it’s a rectangular piece of paper. You can do this using scissors or a utility knife. Place the drink can on a flat, rigid surface, preferably a table.

⚠️⚠️ Do this patiently and carefully, keeping your hand at a safe distance from the cut you are making. Remember that the can is sharp.


Once you have the rectangular sheet cut out, flatten it until you remove as many irregularities as possible from the surface. Imagine it should look like a smooth sheet of paper. This will be the metal sheet we’ll work with from now on.
Using the ruler and the fine-tip marker, draw a 4cm x 4cm square on the metal sheet.

⚠️⚠️ Be careful when making all cuts. If you have them, I recommend using safety gloves.




Step 2 → Turn the can into an antenna

Cut out the 4 cm x 4 cm square you drew with the scissors until you have a square metal sheet.

Now, choose one of the edges of this square sheet and mark the center with a fine-tip marker, that is, 2 centimeters from the edge.
Place the ruler on the center you previously marked and use the marker to make two marks 0.5 cm on each side of the center. Repeat this same step on the opposite edge of the side you are working on. Connect the marks and draw the lines so that you have a 1 cm rectangle.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  


💬❓ How are you doing so far? If your can looks like the last image 👆🏽, we’re on the right track. If not, you can try again following the same steps. No rush, I’ll be here waiting!

Continue drawing marks every 0.5 cm on each of the two lines you already drew. In the end, you should have 7 marks on each of the lines as seen in this image:

Draw lines from side to side for each of the marks you made in the previous step. Then, cut along the 7 lines that remain, without cutting the central column that is 1cm wide.

If your can looks like this 👆🏽, you can proceed to fold one tab, skip one: the second, the fourth, the sixth, and the eighth. Then, you must trim each of the tabs that were folded.
Finally, cover your metal piece on both sides with thick transparent tape; this will allow you to protect it so it lasts.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

We’re done! Now, the easy part: using your can to improve your mobile signal.

Step 3 → Install your antenna on your cell phone
The main antenna of cell phones is usually on the back of your phone, on the upper right side.
Use transparent tape to stick this metal piece in the mentioned place and protect it, preferably, with the phone case you are using.

🎉💪🏽 We’re done! Now you’re ready to enjoy a better signal. Congratulations on finishing this solution; I hope this journey has been challenging and exciting.
Like this one, in Voltaje you can find many more solutions to connect without fear of using the internet as a group. Go ahead and keep browsing! See more solutions →

How do you know if this solution works?

The easiest way is to check if the signal bars or dots on your cell phone (located in the top left or right corner of your screen) change with and without the can. These bars measure how strong the signal you are receiving is. In theory, the more bars you have, the better the signal you should be receiving.
Another option is to measure the download speed on your cell phone. Check out the solution How to test your Internet connection speed? →.
This solution can achieve a significant improvement in your cell phone’s signal reception by one or at most two bars or dots. Keep in mind that the signal cannot improve in places where there has never been a signal.


Other possible Internets
Keep in mind that there are two types of signals: your cell phone → signal, with which you can make calls and send text messages, and the WiFi → signal, with which you can connect to the internet.
With this solution, you can improve both signals because it amplifies the reception and transmission of waves from the antenna built into your cell phone. It’s a little “helping hand” for that antenna. You can try this solution in different conditions and draw your own conclusions about whether it’s working for you or not.
But also, boosting your cell phone signal can help you share internet with other people → who need it. Group internet is safer and can help other people with their work, studies, or enjoying various entertainment activities.
We invite you to be part of a new way of using the internet together! 💪🏽 Boost your signal, enjoy, and share your internet.
Thanks for making it to the end of this solution. We hope it was useful to you! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could benefit from it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

If you want to improve your WiFi modem signal, you can check out this solution: How to improve your router’s signal? →

en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.title: How to improve your modem's signal?
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.summary: Some tips to get the most out of your modem.
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.content:
Hi! I’m Manu, the storyteller from SOLE Colombia, and I’ve also felt super frustrated by losing my internet signal right in the middle of an important meeting or a SOLE session.
What does improving your router signal mean?
Right when you need it most, the connection disappears—has that happened to you? It has to me, more than once. But don’t worry, because you’re about to learn how to improve your Router signal so that happens a lot less often.
Plus, I’ll show you how to optimize your Router → settings so you can browse faster by changing the servers → DNS → and adjusting the WiFi → channel. This isn’t hard, and you can do it right from home! So get ready, because we’re going to get the most out of your network.

What is this for?
I’m going to walk you through how to get the most out of your Router. Together, we’re going to improve the WiFi signal distribution in your space, achieving a more stable connection so it doesn’t fail you when you need it most—whether it’s for a meeting, a class, or a SOLE session. No more interrupted signals when you’re investigating a Big Question!
Remember that these adjustments won’t increase your contracted speed, but they will help the signal reach every corner of your house better by optimizing your DNS.

What do you need?

An internet service that connects through a Router.
The Router’s login credentials.
A computer connected to the network.
A bit of patience (hopefully not too much!).
A “can-do” (cacharrera) attitude.


How to do it?
Alright, I’m going to guide you step-by-step so you can improve your WiFi signal. Trust me! Something is bound to change!

Step 1 → Measure your connection speed

The first thing you need to do is measure your current connection speed. In this solution, we show you how to do it: How to check your internet connection speed? →
Knowing your speed will allow you to compare the “before” and “after” once you’ve made the adjustments.


Step 2 → Explore your space and position the Router

It might seem obvious, but we often forget the simplest things: get closer to the Router. If you’re organizing a SOLE session or have several devices connected, make sure they are as close as possible so the signal reaches them with more strength.
The place where you put the Router is key. Make sure to place it in an elevated spot, like on a table or even mounted on the wall. Ideally, it should be in a central location, not in a corner or near a window, which is where installers often leave it. Moving the Router to a more strategic spot will help the signal spread more evenly throughout the house.

Photo taken from Pexels, (2024).

Photo taken by Manuela Córdoba, (2024).

Step 3 → Place the Router antennas in a perpendicular position

Have you looked at your router’s antennas? Check them right now. An important detail to improve the signal is to make sure they are in a perpendicular position—that is, pointing toward the ceiling. This helps the signal waves distribute better.


Make that adjustment and you’ll notice the difference. Well done!
With these 3 actions, you should already see some kind of improvement. If you want to go further, check out the more advanced steps below.


Step 4 → Configure the DNS

What is that, anyway?
DNS is like an address book that helps your computer find websites faster. By using faster DNS servers, like Google’s or Cloudflare’s, you ensure that pages load with greater speed. Your internet provider’s default servers aren’t always the most optimal, so switching to more efficient ones can improve your browsing experience.
Now we’re going to do something interesting: configure the DNS. This will help the websites you visit load faster, since DNS are the IP address directories that the Router consults when browsing.
If you want to switch to faster and more reliable DNS servers, it will make your internet queries much snappier. To do this, follow these steps:

Access your Router’s administration interface. To do this, in your computer’s network settings, look for the gateway. There you will find an IP address →, something like 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1.
Log in with the credentials, which are usually admin/admin, or check your device’s manual for the default passwords.
Change the values to 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1 (from Cloudflare) and 8.8.8.8 (from Google).
Open your browser and enter that address in the address bar. This will take you to the Router’s control panel.
Look for the Network Settings section, and there, the DNS Servers option.
Save the changes and restart the Router.

Very good! Now your network will use these DNS servers, which are faster and more reliable.


Step 5 → Configure the WiFi channel

Another key adjustment is the WiFi channel configuration. Channels determine the frequency at which the Router emits the signal. To avoid interference with other nearby networks, set your Router to the recommended channels: 1, 6, or 11. To do this:

Enter your Router’s configuration interface again.
Look for the Wireless section.
Choose one of the recommended channels: 1, 6, or 11.
Save the changes and restart the Router.

With this adjustment, you will reduce interference and improve signal quality. Great job, we’re almost done!

How do I know if this solution works?
Did you manage it? I’m sure you did! By following these steps, I’m sure your Router signal has improved, and therefore, the WiFi distribution in your space.

Other possible Internets
Although you won’t be able to increase the speed beyond what you’ve contracted :c, you will have ensured that every corner of your house receives a stronger and more stable signal.
I hope these tips are useful to you and that you no longer have internet cutouts in the middle of an important meeting or an exciting investigation in SOLE.

How to know what type of WiFi signal you have? →
