en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.title: How to install my 3G/4G antenna?
en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.summary: Install an antenna to have Internet in a fixed space.
en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay, and although I’m not an expert on connectivity, I’ve learned by tinkering: that is, through trial and error and asking others about it. Today, I’ll help you install your own antenna!
It’s important to know that there are many types of 3G or 4G antennas, although, in general, this solution should work for installing whichever one you have. Your antenna might come with a manual or instructions. We recommend reading it first. But if you don’t have one, or if the person who sold you the antenna didn’t explain how to do it, what follows might just do the trick!

What does installing a 3G/4G antenna mean?
In short, it’s setting up and getting a device running that allows you to improve cellular signal access in an area where it was previously weak. Keep in mind that for this solution, you need to have the antenna. If you don’t have one yet, you can go to the solution How to buy a 3G-4G antenna? → to find out which one works best for you.

Remember, the instructions and what you find here might look a bit different.


What is it for?
There are places where cellular phone signal is very weak. You can see this in the connection bars on your phone (you might see only one bar or something that says H+, E, or even no signal at all). An antenna with the necessary characteristics for the conditions of the place where you want to connect can help you get better connection quality.
I recently understood that the Internet signal that reaches cell phones travels through invisible electromagnetic waves, and that phones have a small antenna inside that captures those waves, allowing us to access the internet.
What the antenna does is capture and amplify the specific cellular data signal (3G or 4G). In other words, the signal travels in electromagnetic waves through the air from a place higher than where you are—above trees, buildings, or hills—and then comes down through a cable to your level. Once it’s at your level, the signal can be shared over the air using a WiFi network, or by cable using a modem or router.
I know these terms might seem confusing, but as you go through the installation steps, it will become clearer.

Before you start, some safety issues
Remember that you are working with electrical equipment. Be careful when connecting to the power supply. Be aware of weather conditions, especially the risk of storms: at the moment of installation, the antenna could act as a lightning rod. A lightning strike on the antenna could cause serious personal injury and property damage.

What do you need?


The 3G-4G antenna → you purchased.
Coaxial cable → to bring the signal from the antenna.
Modem → with its respective power cable, Ethernet cable, and quick start guide (or instruction manual).
SIM card → from the cellular operator that has the best signal in the area.
Computer with Ethernet connection → and/or WiFi → or smartphone → (Android / iOS).
A tall pole (the same length as the cable or a bit less): it can be a metal pipe, wood, or bamboo. The important thing is that it is as straight as possible and sturdy.
Antenna mounts (which allow you to hang the antenna on the tall pole).
Wrench for tightening nuts.
Materials and tools to secure the pole (depends on where you install it).


How is it done?
This solution has 6 steps, some simpler than others, but don’t worry—if I could do it, you can too. Let’s get started!

Step 1 → Define the place where the antenna and modem will be installed

Before unpacking your purchase, define where you want (or others want) the modem and antenna to be permanently located. If it’s in your home, it could be in the living room. If it’s in a community space, it could be in a room that is secure but where the signal reaches everyone who wants to use it.
Keep in mind that the antenna must be securely attached to the pole, and the pole must be firmly secured somehow outside the house or space. We will explain how later.
The modem needs electricity, so identify the power outlet you are going to connect it to.
Finally, define where you are going to run the cable from the antenna to the space where the modem will be. You might have to drill a hole in the wall so you don’t have to leave a window open. WATCH OUT! Don’t do this until you have verified where the antenna works and connects best.




Step 2 → Identify the mobile phone towers in the area

For antennas to work as well as possible, they must be able to “see” each other or, at least, they should point toward the same place.
If you live in a region with many mountains, it will be a bit more difficult to access a good signal compared to a flat place. If this is your case, your antenna will need more height.
Now identify the nearest phone tower. Look for tall towers with antennas. They are normally located on the peaks of the highest mountains to allow for greater coverage. It is very important that you locate it because that is where your antenna must point.

If you don’t know where the nearest cellular phone tower is, you can also ask your neighbors.

Taken from Wikimedia Commons
🎉 If you made it this far, it means you have already managed to establish the location of the main elements of your solution. That is, you already know…

Where to install your antenna (where it will stay).
Where it should point, that is, toward the nearest phone tower.
Where you will put the modem that will generate the WiFi signal to connect computers or cell phones.

You’re doing great! Now comes the easy part: assembling the antenna.


Step 3 → Insert the SIM and connect the modem to electricity

Open the modem box. It should include a power cable, an Ethernet cable (to connect a computer), and a quick start guide (instructions). Read the guide carefully because every antenna is different. The following steps of this solution should match those in the guide, just in more detail.
Keep in mind that inserting the SIM can be tricky. I had to make several attempts to get it right. Make sure the metallic part of the SIM (the chip) matches the metallic contacts of the modem. I’ll explain it a bit better below.

Identify the SIM card size that matches the modem tray.
First, open the modem cover where the SIM is inserted (usually on the back of the modem). Identify the card size you need to insert. The modem instructions (quick start) will indicate this. The model I have uses the Mini SIM size.

Insert the SIM card into the tray.
You will notice that both the SIM tray and the SIM card have a cut (beveled) corner. This indicates the position in which you must insert the card.

Insert the SIM carefully into the tray and put the cover back on.

Connect the power cable to the modem and the power outlet.
Then, turn on the modem as indicated in the guide. It may be automatic or with a power button.
Check that the modem is connected to the internet.
On the front of the modem, you will find different connection indicators, and the instructions explain what each one means. In the example model, we see that:


The first indicator from left to right shows if it is on or off.
When the second one is red, it means it has no signal. If it is blue or green, it means it is connected. (In this example, it is connected).
The third indicates that the modem is emitting a wireless or WiFi signal in the space.
The fourth shows if an ethernet cable is connected (in this case, no).
And the fifth represents the signal strength (like the signal bars on a cell phone). In this example, the signal is very good.

Once this step is finished, your modem is ready—you’re halfway through the solution! If the connection indicator (the second one in the example) is red, simply turn off the modem and let’s connect the antenna to it.


Step 4 → Connect all the antenna elements and hoist the antenna

The time has come to assemble your antenna. The best way to start is to take out and put together all the elements needed to assemble it. Then, let’s begin.
Adjust the antenna to the highest end of the pole.
Start by adjusting the antenna mount to the base of the antenna using the screws provided for this. Tighten the screws carefully, making sure they are well secured.
Then adjust the antenna mounts to the highest end of the pole. Remember that the pole must be shorter than the length of the cable you have. The mounts have a piece to “wrap” around the pole so that when you tighten the nuts, it grips the pole as shown in the image.


  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

Extend the cable and connect the end that goes to the antenna cable.
Unrolling the cable and extending it to its full length helps make it easier to handle. Look for the connector that fits the antenna connector and connect them.


Find the modem-to-cable connector and connect.
In this modem model, there is a cover on the back of the modem that you must remove with a bit of force (keep the cover in the modem box). There you will find the place to connect the cable. Tighten the connector thread as much as possible, carefully.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

Now you can hoist the antenna with the help of another person and point it toward the phone tower you identified in the second step. Then, turn on the modem and that’s it. You only have two steps left to finish. Bravo! 👏🏽


Step 5 → Connect the computer or cell phone to the modem

Turn on the WiFi on your computer or cell phone and search for the modem’s network. You can usually find the network name on a sticker on the base of the modem. There you will also find the password to connect. Enter the information on your device, and with that, you’re ready to browse the Internet!
If your computer has an Ethernet → port, you can also connect directly by cable. Connecting by cable will always give you the best possible internet browsing speed.

If you managed to connect, go to the next step. If not, read what follows.
Couldn’t connect to the internet? I have some recommendations for you 👇🏽
Sometimes we are in places far from cell phone towers or with a lot of interference between the tower and our antenna. If this is your case, you can try some alternatives.

Enter the modem’s administration webpage and try pointing the antenna in other directions.

Enter your device’s browser (it could be Firefox, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Explorer) and type your modem’s IP address. Generally, you can find this address on the same sticker under the modem. The IP of this modem 👇🏽, for example, is 192.168.8.1.


When you enter that IP address, you will see the modem login page. There, they will ask for the password, which you also find on the sticker. Usually, the password is admin in lowercase.
Then they will ask you some questions to configure your modem’s preferences. Read carefully and select what you think is best. When finished, you will arrive at the modem’s home page where you can check the connection quality and speed.

If the green checkmarks appear, it means everything is connected correctly. On the other hand, if you see a red exclamation mark and an “X” on the internet bars, it means there is no connection.

This is where you must start turning the antenna, trying to point it in another direction until you find a better connection with the cell phone tower. Do it slowly and in small intervals. Also, try pointing it slightly more up or down using the different holes of the antenna-to-pole mount.

Every time you change the position of your antenna, wait a few seconds to see if the indicators on the screen or the device change. If the internet bars and the green check appear, you have managed to get a signal! Congratulations! You can now browse the internet.


💡 How is internet usage measured?
Usage is measured by the amount of data downloaded to your computer or cell phone when making “a query” (for example, watching a video, listening to a song, reading an article in an online newspaper, or receiving a text message). The “weight” of each of those files is measured in bytes of information, and the most common measure when you buy a data plan is Gigas, Gb, or Gigabytes.
Do you know how many things you can do with 1 Giga (1Gb)?



💡 How fast can you access information on the internet?
Just like knowing how much they “weigh,” it is important to know at what speed you can access those files you are querying. This is measured in Megabytes per second or Mbps that are downloaded to your computer or cell phone.
Do you know what speed you need to have certain services?



🧭 Run speed tests
Now that you know about data weight and speed, you can run your own speed test. This will allow you to know how fast data is downloading from the internet. For this, consult the solution How to test your Internet connection speed? →. There you will find the step-by-step guide.


Still can’t connect? 😖 Here are some more advanced recommendations 👇🏽
For greater precision, you can perform signal strength tests by turning the antenna in different directions.
Sometimes geographical conditions are more complex than we imagine. In those cases, we will have to determine if the antenna is effectively connected to the cell phone tower and with what quality.
For that, enter the “Advanced” section in the modem menu and look for “System” and then “Device Information”. That’s how it appears on my modem, but it should be something similar on yours.

In this list of information, you will find several data points. The 4 parameters you are looking for are:

RSRQ, which indicates signal quality;
RSRP, which indicates signal strength;
RSSI, which indicates signal power;
SINR, which indicates the relationship between the signal and the noise being generated.

*Remember that the signal is electromagnetic waves traveling through the air.

Below, you can see a table that indicates the coverage parameters of the cellular signal your antenna is receiving. Note that three of them are negative numbers, and as they get closer to zero, the signal improves. This information might seem a bit technical, but don’t worry, it’s not necessary to understand it in great depth for it to work.








































CoverageRSRQRSRPRSSISINRExcellent> -10 dB> -80 dBm> -65 dBm> 20 dBGood-10 dB to -15dB-80 dBm to -90 dBm-65 dBm to -75 dBm13 dB to 20 dBAverage-15 dB to -20 dB-90 dBm to -100 dBm-75 dBm to -85 dBm0 dB to 13 dBLow< -20 dB< -100 dBm< -85 dBm< -0 dB
*Keep in mind that ”>” means “greater than” and ”<” means “less than”. That is, ”> -10 dB” means “greater than -10dB”.
*Remember that negative numbers work in reverse to positive numbers. For example, -10dB is greater than -80dB (because it is closer to zero).
With this information in mind, what you should do is continue rotating the hoisted antenna in small intervals and wait a few seconds to see how those numbers change.
I mainly look at the RSRP, which is the connection strength. It might be useful to draw a circle on the floor around the antenna pole and draw lines that divide the circle into equal pieces. Then, point the antenna in the direction of each line and check if the parameter improved or worsened. If it improved, keep turning and checking the parameter. If it worsened, go back to the previous point.
This is how the antenna is positioned with greater precision. Good luck capturing the signal! You have become a true internet tinkerer.


💡 Keep in mind that weather affects the signal
As you are using an outdoor antenna, weather conditions might affect how fast or slow your connection is. For example, a very humid day can make your connection slower. Don’t worry, little by little you will improve your internet experience together as you try new solutions.



Step 6 → Secure the antenna

We have reached our last step!
Now, knowing the best direction for the antenna, it is time to install your antenna permanently to a wall, a column, or a tree, in the place you determined in Step 1.
Tighten the antenna mounts to the pole and hoist the antenna
With the help of a wrench, tighten the antenna mounts to the pole firmly to ensure they don’t move with the wind or rain, or if a bird lands on top. If you already had them well tightened, it is not necessary to do this again.


Anchor the pole to the wall or the support you have
Then, use appropriate mounts to anchor the pole to the base. If it’s to a wall, drill and put in anchors and screws to secure it. If it’s to a tree, tie it with wire.


Once fixed, you have finished the installation of a 3G/4G antenna that will allow you to have a WiFi signal in a fixed space.
You are, officially, the “tinkerer” of your home or community. Congratulations! 👷🏽‍♀️🎉👷🏽
Through trial and error, you will feel more and more confident to tinker, that is, to solve by doing. Now, would you be up for doing another solution? Go ahead and keep browsing! See more solutions →

Other possible Internets
Among many connectivity solutions I have tried, this is one of the best for creating a space to access the Internet together, allowing several people to connect at the same time to a WiFi signal in places where the 3G or 4G signal is weak.
I recommend it not only for the home but for common spaces like schools, libraries, businesses, or community halls. It also works in public spaces like parks if they have a place to leave it under lock and key and with constant electricity.

Keep in mind that if there is no mobile phone coverage, this solution will not work. But don’t get discouraged; phone coverage is gradually increasing all over the planet. In the meantime, you can consult another SOLE tool called “The Disconnected” →, where you will find solutions for places where there is no internet.

Although it is not an inexpensive solution (the price of an antenna is between $370 - $400 USD), I have seen that it can have a great impact as it becomes a community internet access point.
For this, the community could agree, buy it with contributions from everyone, and maintain it together. This can result in a considerable initial expense, but in the future, it is cheaper than when each person buys their own individual data plan.


💡 At SOLE Colombia, we have carried out this solution with communities where an antenna is installed in a community space that everyone can access. There, the community decides how much, when, and for what the internet is used. In this way, data top-ups are collectively regulated according to needs and are fully utilized in a shared way.
For example, priority is given to children doing their homework or the community watching a movie together, over individual uses like accessing social networks. This, of course, implies new challenges. But the starting point is clear: you already have internet access!



💬💪🏽 Learn about our experience with a community in Cáceres, Antioquia →



Knowing this, how far would you like to go? Is this a solution you could encourage where you live? We hope it has been useful to you! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could benefit from it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.title: How to know how good your mobile signal is without a speed test?
en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.summary: Types of signal and ways to recognize how good your signal is.
en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.content:
Hi, I’m Manuela. I’m the storyteller for SOLE Colombia, and even though I don’t know much about tech, I’ve started to get a kick out of tinkering with gadgets, and I’m learning all sorts of things that keep me from getting stuck in a bind.
What does it mean to know how good your signal is?
An Internet connection isn’t some ghost that follows us everywhere… or maybe it is a little bit of a ghost!
Here is a way you can learn a bit more about what the Internet is, how to figure out what’s acting up at any given moment, or how to boost your signal.

What is this for?
Knowing how good your Internet connection is can give you clues to understand its performance and troubleshoot potential issues.
For example, it will let you know if the speed you’re paying your mobile or internet provider for is actually what you’re getting… or if they’re pulling a fast one on you.
You can identify the spots in your community, or your house, where you have the best signal. That way, you’ll know where that movie you’re watching is going to buffer, or where you should stand to get a better call.
You’ll be able to make decisions if you need to restart the router →, or change the reception channel for your WiFi → signal. Or even determine if your modem needs an upgrade.
By optimizing your signal, you’ll have a faster and more stable connection to do SOLE or access specific content that requires a better signal.

What do you need?

Your device
To be connected to an Internet signal


How to do it?

Step 1 → Grab your phone and check if you have mobile signal

Look at one of the top corners of your phone. You’ll find some mobile signal bars there: If you see one or more bars, it means the phone is picking up a signal and reading your SIM card →.

Step 2 → How strong is your connection?

Strength is not the same as speed. The little bars measure the RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator), in other words, the power. Think of this like the volume of a voice in a room: when there are more bars, it means someone is speaking loudly; when there are few bars, it means someone is whispering.
However, just because you hear someone loudly doesn’t guarantee they are speaking quickly. Your actual internet speed depends on the bandwidth → available at the tower and how many people are connected at the same time.
The more bars you have, the more power the mobile signal you’re receiving has. You need both, power and speed, to do different things on the Internet. If you don’t have a way to measure your connection speed, you can get an idea of the speed based on the type of connection.


Step 2 → What type of mobile connection do you have and what are they for?

Look next to the mobile signal bars and you’ll see some letters that indicate the type of signal you have. These letters refer to the speeds and technologies that operators use to send you information (Internet data).
Found them? If so, check the list below to see what you can do with each one.

G: Short for GPRS, the slowest of all technologies. It’s a second-generation or 2G network that only allows you to send text messages.
E: Short for EDGE, it’s an improved version of GPRS, also called 2.5G, and it’s useful for simple internet searches.


3G: Also called UMTS, it’s a third-generation network, designed for browsing multimedia content.
H: Uses HSPA technology; it’s something like an improved 3G. It’s more than enough to access social media or listen to music on the Internet.
H+: It’s an evolved HSPA for watching videos online or downloading them more quickly.
4G: This technology is also called LTE, and it’s considered the fourth generation or 4G. The speed of this network reaches 100 Mbps download and 50 Mbps upload, which is what we call “broadband.” Super fast!
5G: It’s the fastest technology of all, for now, and can be 100 times faster than 4G. You need a phone that supports 5G to be able to use it.




Step 3 → How good is your connection?

How many bars do you see? What type of signal do you have? Now that you’ve explored these questions, you can get an idea of how good your connection is without running a speed test. Remember, with the different types of signals you can…

G: only send text messages
E: browse web pages
3G, H, H+: browse social media, listen to music, and watch videos
4G, LTE: have video calls and watch high-definition videos




How to know if this solution works?
If you managed to identify how many signal bars you have and the type of signal, you’ll be able to know how good your connection is, and if you know that, you’ve achieved the goal of this solution!

Other possible Internets
Internet speed tests need… Internet. So, in situations where the connection is very low or slow, the speed meters might not even work. In those cases, this solution is super useful!
It also helps you better understand what the different codes on your phone mean and even helps you get to know the current connectivity situation of the place where you are. If the signal is really bad, you can get your neighbors together to look for spots with a better connection, or even chip in for a shared Internet plan or some other connectivity solution to use the Internet as a group.

en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.title: How to check your internet connection speed?
en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. Until very recently, I didn’t know you could test the speed of your internet connection. I found it super easy and really handy to learn how to do it because it lets me know the status of my connection at any given moment.
Understanding why some things aren’t working for me at certain times gives me peace of mind and helps me look for solutions. Would you like to learn how, too? Let’s get started! 🧭💪🏽

What is an internet speed test?
An internet speed test is a tool that measures how fast your connection is by evaluating your download and upload speeds, as well as your network latency →.

What is it for?
A speed test is useful for a few things.


It’s great for verifying if the speed you’re paying your provider for matches the actual speed you’re getting. This lets you make informed decisions about your internet service provider. For example: Am I really getting what they promised? Is it worth sticking with this provider? Are there others that offer a better connection?


It also helps you identify connection problems, or spots and situations where your signal is better or worse. For example, to 4G antenna →, you need to measure the speed several times until you find the direction where you get the best reception.


Knowing the quality of your internet also lets you know which services you can access. For example, do you know what speed you need to watch a YouTube video? Keep reading to find out! 👇🏽



What do you need?

The device you’re going to connect to the internet with (phone, computer, tablet, etc.)
Access to a website or a measurement app, like “Fast”, “Speedtest”, or nPerf. There are also mobile apps like Speedtest by Ookla.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Access a speed test service

You can run your test right here 👇🏽

  
  
  
    This measurement is made possible by Meter.net
  

If that doesn’t work for you, here are a few more options:

Web services: Fast →, Speedtest →, or nPerf →.
There are also mobile apps like Speedtest by Ookla →.



Step 2 → Run the test

Start the test on the website or app. Wait a few seconds until the number stabilizes.
If you need to take a new measurement, just hit the restart button.

⚠️⚠️ Remember that every time you run a test, you’re using up data. So, if you have a limited data plan, try to run tests only when necessary.



Step 3 → Interpret the results

The results usually show your download speed, upload speed, and latency →. Let me break it down for you:

Download speed: This is the speed at which you receive data from the internet, like when downloading files or watching videos. The higher, the better.
Upload speed: This is the speed at which you send data to the internet, like when sending emails or uploading videos to social media. Here, too, the higher, the better.
Latency (ping): This is the time it takes for a signal to travel back and forth between your device and a remote server →, measured in milliseconds.
Here, a lower ping is better, especially for online gaming, video calls, or high-quality videos.


💬❓ Now for the big question: how much speed is enough? Click on this link → to find out how much speed you need to access different services.

Now that you know your internet speed and the speed you need for different services, you can see more solutions → that will allow you to get, improve, or share your internet.


Additional considerations:

Wired connection → vs. WiFi →: Speed tests via cable (Ethernet) are usually more accurate than WiFi tests, as WiFi connections can be affected by interference.
Test servers →: Some services let you choose the test server to get more accurate results or to test different locations.
Interpreting results: Compare your results with the speed you’re paying for and consider factors like the time of day and the activity on your network →, as these can affect the numbers.


How do you know if this solution works?
If you managed to find the upload, download, and latency values of your internet connection, you’ve completed the first part of the solution. Congrats!
Beyond the technical side, this solution works when it allows people like you to:

Verify internet connection performance, giving you more information to make decisions, for example, regarding your internet provider.
Diagnose connection problems to, for example, identify places where the connection is better or worse.
Optimize your online experience, so you can adjust your activities based on what you need. For example, you can avoid downloading heavy files during peak hours, close windows you aren’t using, or disconnect devices to avoid overloading the modem.


Other possible Internets
Diagnosing connectivity status in remote contexts is essential for knowing which type of connectivity solution is best suited for each context.

For us at SOLE, it has been very important to know how to do this when we work with communities. We’ve discovered that having a complete internet experience—where people learn to recognize their own connection conditions, as well as the fluctuations and issues typical of the place where a solution is being installed—encourages people to get more engaged. It’s a very powerful and intense strategy for promoting self-organized learning.
Feeling capable of setting up or improving the internet signal so it can be used as a group makes everything more powerful… you can see the stories in the inspirations section → of Voltaje ⚡⚡.

If you’re connected to WiFi, we have some recommendations to help you make the most of your internet: How to make the most of my bandwidth? →

en/solve/solv-jangala-install-box.summary: Guide to get your Jangala up and running.
en/solve/solv-jangala-install-box.content:
Hi! My name is Catalina. I recently came across the Jangala Big Box, and I think it’s a brilliant connectivity solution! This is the first solution I’m writing to share on Voltaje. It’ll be short and sweet; I hope you find it useful. Let’s get started!

What is installing a Jangala Big Box?
A Jangala Big Box is a very powerful modem that can capture different types of signals and redistribute them to up to 100 people.
In this solution, I’ll walk you through accessing the Big Box installation manual, where you’ll find instructions on how to link different signal sources (SIM cards, wired antennas, among others) to the device.

What is it for?
To install the Jangala Big Box yourself and enjoy the internet, as a community.

💬⚠️ Keep in mind that you need to have a Jangala for this solution to be useful. Check out the solution “Internet in a box: Jangala’s Big Box” → to learn how to get a Jangala Big Box.


What do you need?

A Jangala Big Box.
A device to connect to the internet (cell phone, tablet, computer, or any other).
An internet connection.
Your full attention.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Go to the Jangala website and choose the manual in the language you prefer.

Go to the instructions section of the Jangala website by clicking on this link →.
Once you’re there, you’ll see several blue buttons. Choose the one in your preferred language (Spanish?). A new window will open, and you’ll be able to see the instructions.


Step 2 → Download the instructions

It’s possible that the place where you’re checking this information (good connectivity) isn’t the same place where you’re going to install your Jangala (low connectivity).
If that’s your case, you can download the instructions to your phone or computer so you always have them handy.

How do you know if this solution works?
If you manage to turn on your Jangala and connect to the internet from a couple of devices, you’ll know your hard work paid off!

Other possible Internets
Getting a super powerful internet connection up and running in your community!! Not just because you’ll have a stronger signal, but because it allows so many people to get online.
The next step is to use the internet as a group to learn, create, and transform. In the related solutions (at the end of this article 👇🏽), we recommend some solutions that might be useful for learning how to take care of and share equipment as a community.
Is this a solution that could help others? We hope that, at the very least, it was useful to you! And if it was, share it with others!

en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.title: "The internet in a box: Jangala's Big Box"
en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.summary: Manage and configure a powerful wireless internet router.
en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay, and even though I’m not a connectivity expert, I’ve learned by tinkering—that is, through trial and error, researching online with others, and learning from those who have the experience. Let me briefly tell you what the Jangala Big Box is all about 👇🏽

Video conceived, created, and produced by SOLE Colombia, 2024
What does it mean to manage a Jangala Big Box?
With this solution, you’ll be able to reach out to an organization in England that offers a very powerful portable modem called the Big Box, which allows up to 100 people to connect to the internet at the same time.
The organization that offers it is called Jangala, and they are dedicated to providing internet access to people who need urgent humanitarian aid or support for long-term development projects.

⚠️⚠️ It’s important to know that these devices are not for personal use and you must meet certain eligibility criteria. They are the ones who, based on the information you provide in the application form, evaluate whether your community or project can access their product.

We encourage you to get together with your community and imagine how an internet connection could improve your living conditions and how you can use it for the common good. Develop the idea and share it with Jangala. We’re sure they’ll consider it.

What is it for?
Imagine a community without connectivity, without the technical knowledge to install, configure, or maintain a wireless network. Now, think about how, all of a sudden, everyone manages to connect to a single WiFi → network. What would happen?
Among many things, an entire community could pay for a single internet plan and share the connection. Even better, they could do it from common devices like computers or tablets, enjoying higher speeds, a better experience, and a collective, fun learning process.
That’s what you could achieve if you manage to get this device: the Big Box from Jangala.
The Jangala Big Box is a lightweight, briefcase-sized device that transforms any form of internet connectivity into a WiFi network that is easy to manage and scale, from dozens to thousands of users. It’s like having a signal booster for a phone’s internet that can serve hundreds, or even thousands, of computers.
Internet access is an urgent need in many situations around the world: from people trying to make contact after an earthquake to educational projects in remote areas. However, in these contexts, the internet is often unavailable. Networks tend to go down in emergencies, and deploying effective internet access in remote areas is complicated, slow, and expensive.
Who is Jangala? Jangala is a UK-based NGO that seeks to solve this with their machines.
This solution will help you learn how to manage this powerful modem with the Jangala organization and receive their support to adapt the Big Box to the needs of your context or, if you are part of an organization, to the conditions of the communities you work with.
If you are a low-income community or located in a remote area, you may be considered to receive one of their units at no cost, for life.

What do you need?

An internet connection and a computer (you can also use a cell phone).
To understand English or use the online translator DeepL.
Confidence in your management skills.
Conditions of digital exclusion; Jangala will assess if you are eligible to receive a Big Box.
Enthusiasm!


How to do it?

Step 1 → Go to www.janga.la and look for the Big Box application form

Go to Jangala get box and head to the “Request a Box” section. There, you can decide if what you need is a Get Box, which is smaller, or a Big Box.
The following steps refer to the Big Box application.



Step 2 → Fill out the online form

In the Big Box section, you will find a button that says Apply for a Big Box.
You need to answer the questions in the form; this will help Jangala configure a Big Box that best meets your community’s needs.
The questionnaire is divided into four sections:

Section 1 asks questions about you and/or your organization.
Section 2 is about the place where you need the Big Box, including location, existing connectivity, and power supply.
Section 3 is about the Wi-Fi configuration.
Section 4 contains final questions about how the Big Box will make a difference.

If anything in this form is unclear or doesn’t apply to your community’s situation, don’t hesitate to send an email to info@janga.la.
Filling out this form can take some time, and you might not have all the answers ready. Try to answer as many questions as possible to the best of your ability, and don’t forget to press the “Submit” button.


Step 3 → Wait for a response and build a relationship with Jangala

It may take a few weeks to hear back from the Jangala team. They will write to the email address you registered in the form.
Be patient and keep an eye out for their reply… that moment will be very exciting!
It is possible that they will have more questions or that a virtual meeting with you will be required. During the meeting, you can clarify any further doubts, define the specifics of your Big Box, and the process by which you will receive it via postal mail.
The Jangala team is exceptional: always very kind and genuinely willing to help.


Step 4 → Plan and receive the Big Box by mail

After clarifying how Jangala will send the equipment, it won’t take more than a couple of weeks to receive the Big Box with the features you need.
It is very important to ask the Jangala team to clearly state on the certified mail shipping label that it is goods with no commercial value, because, depending on the country you are in, customs may require specific information about the equipment to release the package.
For example, in Colombia, to import a cell phone, it is necessary to include the IMEI number (used to register a phone) on the shipping invoice. If this isn’t done, you have to clear the package through customs, which is a complex and expensive process. Regardless, the Jangala team will be a great support in solving any challenge, and they cover those costs.


Step 5 → Install the Big Box

Finally, all that’s left is to install the Big Box → in the place where it will be used, and that’s it!
The Jangala team will offer you support during installation or use. Once installed, you will have WiFi internet for about 100 people within a 100-meter radius!
Now, all that’s left is to use it for the common good.

How do you know if this solution works?
You’ll know the day you receive a response from Jangala. Regardless of whether the answer is positive or not, just receiving it is proof that you managed the process correctly, and that is already a great achievement!
If you are a charitable organization or a group that needs connectivity for a common purpose, Jangala would love to meet you. Jangala can provide devices and tools in the form of long-term, no-cost loans to organizations with limited financial means that provide vital basic services to people affected by disasters, or to organizations that need help with long-term development projects.
Remember that any of the Boxes provide WiFi through any form of internet signal (3G/4G, landline, satellite), can use power from various sources (mains, battery, cigarette lighter, renewable source, generator), and can use an external antenna → to pick up 3G/4G signals where phones cannot.

How many people does it connect? 100. With additional equipment, it can reach up to 1,000. With extensive equipment, up to 5,000.
Can it be used in a mobile environment? Yes.
Can it be used outdoors? Yes. It is waterproof and rugged.
Can it power additional Wi-Fi access points? Yes. They can be used to connect up to 5,000 people in a large area.
How many networks can it broadcast? Four. Each of them can be customized in terms of content control, speed restrictions, and data limits.




💡 At SOLE Colombia, we have implemented this solution with communities where an antenna is installed in a community space that everyone can access. There, the community decides how much, when, and what the internet is used for.
For example, priority is given to children doing their homework or the community watching a movie together, over individual uses like accessing social media. This, of course, involves new challenges. But the starting point is clear: you already have internet access!

💬💪🏽 Learn about our experience with a community in Nuevo México, Santander de Quilichao →



Other possible Internets
The Jangala Big Box is an opportunity to get free or very low-cost connectivity for an entire community. For example, a school or a refugee camp. Imagine the learning possibilities you would have if you use the internet together!

⚠️⚠️ Mind you, keep in mind that the Jangala Big Box will not solve connectivity issues if there is no internet signal (cable, mobile, or satellite) in the area.


Related solutions

Remember that the Jangala Big Box needs some kind of signal to work. If you do it through a SIM Card (cellular signal), this solution can help you decide which internet plan to buy: How do I buy the right cell phone plan for me? →
Having a “Big Box” means we must take care of it as a community. Using a playful tool, you can learn to do it together: How to use games to learn how to take care of equipment as a community? →
Community internet is more powerful when used in a group. I share some recommendations for finding a meeting space: How to set up a space to use the internet as a group? →

Remember that at Voltaje ⚡⚡ you can find many more solutions to connect without fear of using the internet as a group. Go ahead and keep browsing! See more solutions →

en/solve/solv-know-ram.title: "How to know how much RAM I have?"
en/solve/solv-know-ram.summary: "Learn how to check your computer's memory to see if it is ready for new tasks."
en/solve/solv-know-ram.content:
Hi! I’m David. I’ve managed to get a better handle on how my gear works through trial and error, and today I want to share a quick way to peek under the hood of your computer. We’ll lean on what we already know and confirm a few steps with some digital tools so you can’t go wrong.

What is RAM?
RAM → is like a kitchen assistant with a short-term memory. Imagine your computer is a kitchen: the RAM is the countertop.
The assistant is super fast at handing you the ingredients you need right now on the counter, but as soon as you turn off the stove (the computer), she clears everything off and forgets what she was doing.
If your counter is too small (low RAM), the assistant gets crowded with pots and pans, and everything slows down. That’s why knowing how much memory you have is key to keeping your gear from getting bogged down.

What is it for?
Knowing how much RAM you have lets you figure out if your computer can handle running many programs at once or if it’s going to “choke” on heavy tasks like videos or games.

What do you need?

Your computer (Windows or Mac →) turned on.
A couple of minutes of peace and quiet.


How to do it?
First, identify if your machine is Windows or Mac →.
On Windows (10 and 11)

Step 1 → The quick way: Settings

Press the Windows + i keys on your keyboard (the ‘i’ stands for information). A settings window will pop up.

If you have Windows 10: Go to “System” and look for “About” at the bottom of the left-hand menu.
If you have Windows 11: Go to “System” and look for the “About” option at the end of the list.

Look for where it says “Installed RAM”. You’ll see a number there like 4GB, 8GB, or 16GB.


Step 2 → The administrator’s path (to see real-time usage)

If you want to see how much work the “assistant” has on her plate right now:

Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc all at once.
Click on the Performance tab and then on Memory.

Here you’ll see how much memory you’re using and how much is left over.


You’re on the right track: If you see the graph is very high (near the top), it means your “countertop” is full of pots and dishes.

On Mac computers (Apple →)

Step 1 → The Apple menu

Click the Apple icon () in the top-left corner of your screen and select “About This Mac”.
A small window will open where you’ll clearly see the word Memory.


Step 2 → Using the Terminal (for the curious)

If you want to feel like a pro, you can use the Terminal →.

Open the Terminal (find it in Spotlight with Cmd + Space).
Type the command: vm_stat and press Enter.

This will show you a lot of technical info, including the use of Swap Memory →.

What is Swap Memory? It’s like when the assistant runs out of space on the counter and starts using a drawer in the pantry (the hard drive) → to store dishes. It’s slower than the counter, but it helps keep the kitchen from coming to a complete halt.


Recommendations…

If you have 4GB of RAM, try not to have too many browser tabs open at the same time.
With 8GB, you can comfortably handle most office and study tasks.
If you notice your machine is always using “Swap,” it might be time to think about upgrading your physical RAM or switching to an SSD if your computer allows it.


How do you know if this solution works?
If you managed to find the number (e.g., 8 GB) and understand whether you’re using a lot or a little, congratulations! You know your work tool a bit better now.

Other possible Internets
By knowing how much RAM you have, you stop getting frustrated when the computer slows down and start making decisions: Should I close this program? Do I need to upgrade my gear? Can I install this game?

Recommended solutions

Why is my internet slow? →
Give your old computer a second life →

Keep tinkering—that’s how you really learn!

en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.title: How to find the WiFi passwords on my cell phone?
en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.summary: Find (and share) the passwords saved on your cell phone.
en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.content:
slug: solv-know-wifipasswords
Hi, I’m Belén. I’m no tech expert, but I’ve learned how to use it as it’s come along. I won’t lie to you, I actually like reading the manuals for the gadgets I buy, and I make it my business to understand many of the updates that get installed on my mobile phone… total nerd alert!

What does it mean to know your phone’s WiFi passwords?
I remember when you had to type in the modem password every single time you connected to the Internet. If there’s one thing I appreciate about this new era of smartphones, it’s the time saved by not having to type in the WiFi key every time you connect. But where are they stored? How can you share those keys or passwords with someone else? Keep reading 👇🏽

What is it for?
With this solution, you’ll be able to explore the WiFi → passwords already stored on your phone.
If you want to do a SOLE in a place where you’ve been connected before, you can reconnect to the WiFi network without having to re-enter every single character of the password (which is sometimes super long or really complicated).

What do you need?

A phone with an Android operating system →.
An Internet connection.
At least one WiFi password saved on your phone.
Curiosity.
Attention to detail.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Explore your passwords

First, go to your phone’s “Settings.” Then, head to the WiFi section, where you’ll see all the networks available around you. Tap on the Internet network you already have access to and whose password you want to find. Once you do, a QR code with this information will appear. Take a screenshot of this image.



Step 2 → Decipher the password

The next step is to use a reader that has permission to read this information. We can’t use our own phone’s QR reader for this, so we can use an online one on the following page: Zxing

Once we’re on this page, we upload our image and click the “Submit Query” button. Doing this will show us the network name and the password so we can share it.



Step 3 → You’re ready to share!

Now, all that’s left is to share this info with the folks who need it. Who’s up for doing a SOLE →? Now that you can share the password, everyone’s devices can start their research and solve whatever Big Question they want!

How do you know if this solution works?
With this solution, you’ll be able to explore all the WiFi passwords you already have saved on your phone.

Other possible Internets
You can find the keys you’ve already saved, but not the ones you haven’t saved yet. To save them initially, you have to ask the WiFi owner to share their key with you, but after that, you won’t have to ask again.
Now that you know the whole process, is this a solution that could help others? We hope it was at least useful to you! And if it was, share it with others!
See you soon! 👋🏽

Related solutions

It might be useful to look for WiFi signals around you using a mobile app. Here we explain how: What free networks are available for me to connect to the internet? →
If you can’t find passwords and what you wanted was for someone else to connect, you can also share your own internet! How to share Internet from my phone? →

Remember that at Voltaje ⚡⚡ you can find many more solutions to connect without fear of using the internet in a group. Keep on surfing! See more solutions →
